title: Way to Be!: 9 Ways To Be Happy And Make Something Of Your Life
author: Gordon B. Hinckley
target_audience: People seeking moral and ethical guidance
Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS)
General readers interested in character development
core_themes: Cultivating core values for a meaningful life
primary_purpose: To give readers—especially young people—practical, value-based principles to guide them toward happiness and success in life by cultivating nine essential character traits.

structure_format.narrative_style: Encouraging, accessible, and conversational with wisdom and anecdotes
structure_format.organization: Divided into nine chapters, each focusing on a 'Be' value (e.g., Be Grateful, Be Smart), plus an introduction and conclusion

key_concepts_lessons: True happiness is found through living with integrity and purpose.
Character is built by consistently choosing virtuous behaviors.
Nine core 'Be's—Grateful, Smart, Clean, True, Humble, Prayerful, Positive, Still, Involved—can guide life decisions and actions.
Adopting positive habits shapes not just individual lives, but also communities and the wider world.
Overcoming challenges relies on strong foundational values.
Spirituality and faith enrich daily living and personal fulfillment.
notable_features: Simple, memorable framework built around the '9 Be's'
Faith-informed guidance with broad, universal appeal
Suitable for both secular and religious audiences
cultural_historical_context: Written by Gordon B. Hinckley, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, shortly after the turn of the millennium. The book addressed concerns about moral direction in a rapidly changing society and aimed to provide a positive, principle-centered anchor for youth.
reception_impact: Popular within LDS and broader Christian circles for its practical wisdom
Praised for its accessibility, warmth, and relevance to young readers
Embraced by parents and educators as a tool for teaching values
Some secular critics find the advice generic or overtly religious, but core principles are widely considered universal
comparable_titles: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens by Sean Covey
Make Your Bed by Admiral William H. McRaven
Dare to Lead by Brené Brown
The Road to Character by David Brooks
